narrative:
The model predicts you have a 32% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your chances of success.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. By far the strongest factor is your history of three past class failures. While students who passed had zero previous failures on average, your record of repeated setbacks strongly signals to the model that you are at much higher risk this year.

Two other factors pulled the prediction in the opposite direction, making failure less likely than it otherwise would have been. Your father’s job being at home and having a guardian who is neither parent both worked in your favor. These characteristics are relatively uncommon among students who ultimately pass, and the model sees them as offering some protective influence, perhaps through extra availability or different family dynamics.

Even with these mitigating elements, your past academic failures outweighed them. To improve, you should treat this as an early warning: focus immediately on consistent study habits, seek extra academic support, and address any underlying reasons that led to those earlier failures. Taking the remedial courses seriously is a practical first step toward changing the outcome. (218 words)
